# Outline and Contour Generation

Also called: Outline Generation, Contour Rendering, Edge Highlighting

## Overview
Outline and Contour Generation is a non-photorealistic volume rendering technique that enhances perceptual clarity by rendering view-dependent or feature-based lines that demarcate object boundaries, silhouettes, or internal structures [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial]. It sets itself apart from standard Direct Volume Rendering (DVR) by relying on gradient magnitude, viewing angle, or topological properties rather than voxel intensity values alone, allowing for faster parameter tuning and clearer shape conveyance [S2, unofficial]. Unlike surface-based NPR, which assumes well-defined surfaces, this family handles volumetric features that vary continuously in 3D space by analyzing local volumetric properties [S2, unofficial][S4, unofficial].

## Shared principles
The family shares the fundamental goal of enhancing perceptual clarity through non-photorealistic edge representation. Common mechanisms include:
1.  **Edge Detection:** Identifying boundaries based on geometric properties (normals, curvature, topology) or image-space properties (depth, normal discontinuities) [S2, unofficial][S3, S4, unofficial].
2.  **Line Rendering:** Converting detected edges into line primitives (strips, segments) or stylized strokes [S2, unofficial][S3, S4, unofficial].
3.  **Compositing:** Integrating these lines with the underlying volume or surface rendering, often using depth buffering for hidden line removal [S2, unofficial][S3, S4, unofficial].

Volumetric illustration differs from surface-based NPR in several important ways [S2, unofficial][S4, unofficial]. In surface NPR, surfaces (features) are well-defined, whereas with volumes, feature areas within the volume must be determined through analysis of local volumetric properties because volumetric features vary continuously throughout three-dimensional space [S2, unofficial][S4, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [Object Contour NPR](787-object-contour-npr.md)
Object Contour NPR generates view-dependent lines that demarcate areas where an object's surface turns away from the viewer, conveying shape by emphasizing boundaries. Unlike hatches, which are often pre-rendered to texture buffers, these contours are traced directly to the screen using geometry shaders. It differs from standard Direct Volume Rendering (DVR) by relying exclusively on gradient magnitude and viewing angle rather than voxel intensity values, allowing for faster parameter tuning.

### [Lasso Contour Rendering](1855-lasso-contour-rendering.md)
Lasso Contour Rendering is an interactive, pixel-based outline generation method that allows users to manually define regions of interest within a volume using a freehand "lasso" selection tool. Unlike automatic contour methods that detect edges based on scalar field gradients, this approach relies on user intent to highlight specific structures. It is distinguished by its integration into a real-time rendering pipeline where the contour is rendered dynamically only when the user is actively drawing, leveraging offscreen render passes to composite the selection overlay.

### [Curvature-Controlled Style Contours](5350-curvature-controlled-style-contours.md)
Curvature-Controlled Style Contours is a non-photorealistic volume rendering technique that generates outline contours with consistent apparent thickness by regulating the detection threshold based on the normal curvature along the view direction. Unlike standard dot-product contours which produce uncontrolled thickness variations (too thick on flat surfaces, too thin on fine structures), this method ensures that contours remain perceptually uniform across varying surface geometries. It builds on [Outline and Contour Generation](4137-outline-and-contour-generation.md) by integrating curvature-aware edge detection with style transfer functions to map contour appearance to surface properties.

### [Silhouette Rendering](7959-silhouette-rendering.md)
Silhouette rendering is an object-space line rendering technique that extracts and stylizes significant edges (silhouettes and feature lines) to enhance perceptual clarity and discriminate object classes based on specific features. It sets itself apart from image-space methods by processing geometry data directly, allowing for independent stylization of strokes and robust hidden line removal via z-buffer comparison.

### [Topological Landscape](8481-topological-landscape.md)
Topological landscape is a visualization technique that maps the topological structure of a scalar field onto a 3D terrain model to enhance perceptual clarity of data connectivity. It sets itself apart from standard contour rendering by transforming abstract topological events (merges and splits) into intuitive geometric features (peaks and valleys) that leverage human spatial reasoning.

### [Boundary Enhancement Volume Style](10863-boundary-enhancement-volume-style.md)
Boundary Enhancement Volume Style is a non-photorealistic rendering technique designed to highlight feature bounds and reduce noise in volume visualization. It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [Object Contour NPR](787-object-contour-npr.md) and [Silhouette Rendering](7959-silhouette-rendering.md) by operating directly on the volume data to enhance internal boundaries rather than relying solely on surface extraction or image-space silhouette detection. It is typically composed with other styles, such as [ShadedVolumeStyle](4137-outline-and-contour-generation.md#ShadedVolumeStyle), within a [ComposedVolumeStyle](4137-outline-and-contour-generation.md#ComposedVolumeStyle) node.

### Image Space Outline Generation
#### definition
- [S1, unofficial] A pixel-based method to generate simple outlines by extracting edges from depth or normal maps, observing that depth differences are minimal between adjacent pixels of a single object and large between objects, and normals vary smoothly across a single surface but show discontinuity between surfaces.
#### step
- [S1, unofficial] Extract edges from a depth map or normal map using an edge detection mechanism, such as the Sobel filter.
- [S1, unofficial] Combine detected depth and normal edges to yield perceptually significant silhouettes.
- [S1, unofficial] For further processing (e.g., modifying line qualities), calculate analytical curves from the detected edge map, as detected edges only exist as lists of pixels.
#### comparison
- [S1, unofficial] Depth edges reflect C0 discontinuities, while normal edges reflect C1 discontinuities; combining both yields all perceptually significant silhouettes in the source model.

### Ghosted Views with Contours
#### step
- [S2, unofficial] Pre-segment the most interesting internal structures (e.g., small internal organs).
- [S2, unofficial] Identify context information (e.g., the body) that obscures the interesting structures.
- [S2, unofficial] In areas of occlusion, reduce the visual representation of the context object to contours.

## Background
The concept of using outlines to enhance shape perception in computer graphics has roots in early non-photorealistic rendering surveys. Hertzmann presented a useful survey of image space outline generation algorithms in [Her99], noting that pixel-based methods are generally faster and simpler to implement than analytical methods [Str98, p. 106]. Schlechtweg and Raab described a flexible line model where the path is expressed using parametric curves, with style attributes mapped to visual properties like width and brightness [Str98, p. 80-83].

In the context of volume visualization, illustrative techniques have been applied to medical and scientific data to improve clarity. Straka et al. applied cut-away techniques for CT-angiography to visualize peripheral arteries, emphasizing the need for clear views of vessels and surrounding structures like bones and skin [SvC* 04]. More broadly, expressive visualizations inspired by illustration techniques are useful for various visualization tasks, including the visualization of multidimensional volumetric data such as hurricane moisture clouds [S2, unofficial].
